MADE FOR THE LOVE OF FLIGHT

FLIGHT RECORDER

FOXTRAIL 64

An original arcade flight adventure inspired by StarFox 64. You are Vix, the newest pilot in a small squadron defending the Aster Coast from an automated sky fortress.

All aircraft, landscapes, characters, effects, sound design and music are created procedurally for this game. No source-game assets, names, dialogue or music are used.

Built with Three.js R180, WebGPU only, TSL cel shading, Rapier 0.19.3, Web Audio and the Gamepad API. Fonts: Space Grotesk and Barlow Condensed, Google Fonts / SIL Open Font License.

Last reported usage (final provider event missing). Usage: Session time 59m 45s; tokens 6,170,838 total (6,068,530 input including 5,895,680 cached and 0 cache-write; 102,308 output including 32,147 reasoning); API cost $1.958348 USD (Estimated standard API token cost; not subscription billing).

ENGINE FEEDBACK

Liked most: TSL brings banded cel lighting and animated ocean shading into the same WebGPU pipeline.

Got stuck or guessed wrong: Headless WebGPU support and rendering behavior required explicit browser validation.

Built ourselves: A mission director tying corridor flight, free flight, checkpoints, wingmates, boss stages and the attract pilot together.

Hardest part: Reliable WebGPU-only startup and deterministic browser verification.

Overhaul: Make automatic backend fallback explicitly opt-in. One change: A supported game template with input, audio and fixed-step physics conventions.

PROMPT FEEDBACK / 404299fcd4

Liked most: Controller-first navigation and a real attract mode give the demo a clear arcade identity.

Confusing: “Unlimited” performance leaves the target hardware undefined; rendering still depends on the player’s GPU.

Hardest: Completing a readable, coherent mission with multiple flight modes, combat mechanics, and all its support systems in one HTML file.

One additional test: A living-room session with a physical PS5 controller, including disconnecting and reconnecting it during a boss fight.

Known limitations: No known gameplay blockers. Engine dependencies and fonts are embedded. A WebGPU-capable browser and controller or keyboard are required.
